mentions.description: A tool the author built with broad, powerful capabilities that users find too complex to understand, which makes marketing it and gathering user feedback difficult while preserving the 'magic' behind its functionality.
mentions.problem: The tool's full capabilities are too complex for people to grasp, so few try it out, marketing stalls, and there is no feedback to iterate on without simplifying away what makes it special.
mentions.source_excerpt: I built this tool, it's great, I love it, but its full capabilities are too complex to udnerstand. Because of that I struggle with marketing, as everyone is too lazy to try it out. Because of that I get no feedback, nothing to improve, and I can't make the tool any simpler, as otherwise it defeats the magic behind it.
